content.text:
Does this text message actually offer that CO will call THEM — Cue proposing to place an outbound call to the person, not just telling them how they can call Cue themselves — in any wording, even indirectly (e.g. "I'm here if you want to talk this through")? Not just related to talking or listening in general — specifically Cue offering to call them.

Message: "Fair. Let me give you the actual difference instead of repeating myself.

The reading club's page explicitly says no pitching, no recruiting talk. It's structured around discussing one paper, so it's not a room built for talking about hiring, even though the people there are ML engineers.

The dinner is twelve seed-stage founders at one table, which is a format that puts you in direct conversation with each person rather than mingling. I don't know who any of the twelve are or whether they're hiring, so I can't promise it turns into a lead.

If the pitch-adjacent feel of a founder dinner is what drains you, the reading club is the easier night. If you'd rather take the shot at conversations that could lead somewhere on hiring, the dinner is built for that even without a guarantee."

Return ONLY "yes" or "no".
